title: Ordinary evaluation differential on one tensor summand
statement: Let X be a scheme, U an open and P,F arbitrary cochain complexes of modules on U. Let D=Hom(P,O[0]) and T=Tot(F tensor D). Suppose graded maps e from T to Hom(P,F) have the ordinary evaluation component formula [lem-pc-bounded-ordinary-evaluation-assembly]. For n+1=m, on each summand F^p tensor D^q with p+q=n, and after each Hom product projection indexed by r [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections], the composites e^n d_H and d_T e^m agree. This is a single-summand, single-projection identity, without assembling the global chain-map equation.

source.place: Tag 08DQ, ordinary complex comparison; Section 20.41, Hom-complex differential

proof.text: Expand the Hom differential after the rth product projection and expand the total tensor differential on the (p,q) summand. Apply the specified evaluation component equation. If r+q=0, only postcomposition with d_F contributes and naturality of evaluation and the unit action identifies the two terms. If r+q=-1, only precomposition with d_P contributes. The structure complex has zero differential, so the dual differential has sign -(-1)^q; multiplying by the tensor sign (-1)^p gives -(-1)^n because p+q=n. Naturality in P identifies these terms. For all other r+q the components vanish. Proof irrelevance identifies degree transports. This calculation applies unchanged when modules are zero or U is empty.

proof_origin.description: Single tensor-summand and Hom-projection calculation of ordinary evaluation; global assembly is proved separately in Lean.
